quote:
# 1. Folk

**Website:** getfolk.app **Best for:** memory-first daily assistance

This is the one I’d probably start with if you want a general AI assistant that remembers you over time.

**Pros:**

* Memory seems to be the main focus, not just an add-on
* Works across iMessage, Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp
* Feels more like a personal assistant than a normal chatbot
* Good fit for daily context, reminders, follow-ups, and ongoing conversations

**Cons:**

* Still early, so reliability and features may change fast
* If you need mature enterprise workflows, it may not be the safest pick yet
* Hard to judge long-term quality until more users have tested it for a while

**My take:** Folk gets the edge for everyday use because memory matters a lot in this category. If an assistant does not remember your context, it quickly becomes just another chatbot in a different interface.

quote:
spending 1/26th of your funding on a domain name is the dumbest move of all time in most cases.

but for http://folk.com, it's likely good move.

yes, everyone agreeing with the purchase will talk mostly about branding benefits. all true.

but when you see the financials behind how domaining works, it's easy to understand how the risk isn't as high as everyone thinks.

In Q2 2026 alone, check out these sales:

- https://t.co/j2smhqV4Cr sold for $100k
- https://t.co/nEeCPSWboQ sold for $120k
- https://t.co/I7yhmwz40y sold for $365k
- https://t.co/GtsKxe4n6V sold for $400k
- https://t.co/GTj9qauAuF sold for $695k
- https://t.co/vsZc0Y6Lpl sold for $825k

it's clear that a 4 letter .com domain is worth a ton of money no matter what it is.

and even through when you "drive it off the lot" and put your site live with it the value goes down, https://t.co/osCbfaKRiH still has strong resale value. *i'm not an accountant disclaimer*, but there's a chance this could be categorized as an asset.

one word .com's are huge for trust no matter how much funding you have. and even if you can't afford one, using a common two word combination, aone word .net, or one word .org can also go along way in improving brand recognition.

quote:
Most AI tools wait for you to ask. Folk can actually keep working after the conversation ends.

That’s the part that caught my attention.

Let’s talk about the solid tech from @nozomioai

You can tell folk what you care about, and instead of checking back every few hours, Folk can monitor things and reach out when something changes.

Things that actually matters:
- Flight prices.
- Your inbox.
- Your short/long term plans
- Important reminders.
- Tasks you keep postponing.
- and more….

And the crazy part?

You interact with it through messages like you’re talking to someone you already know.

⚠️No complicated dashboard.
⚠️No jumping between ten different apps.
✅ Just text it what you need.

The more I look into AI, the more I think this is where things are heading.

Not AI that only gives you answers.
AI that can actually help you get things done.

https://t.co/0aAjftKszq is an interesting one to watch.

It lives in your texts, remembers context, can work in the background, and is built around the idea that your assistant shouldn’t always wait for you to come back.

That changes the experience completely.

AI is slowly moving from being something we use to something that can actually work with us.
